xsync-status(7) ​

Development status

Current capabilities and remaining work, reviewed against the project backlog.

SCOPE ​

Reviewed 10 October 2026 against the current README, executable help, daily-driver backlog, performance roadmap, and GUI backlog. Earlier backlog problem statements are historical; the latest status and completion entries describe the implemented CLI.

NOTE

This page describes development status. Planned capabilities are not part of the command reference.

IMPLEMENTED CLI ​

AreaCurrent status
Trust hardeningAll 15 P0 stories recorded complete
Reach and everyday CLIR-02–R-09 and E-01–E-13 recorded complete (21 of 22 P1 stories); R-01 remains partial
ProgressP2 closed: U-02–U-11 recorded complete; U-01 skipped at the user’s request
Executable nameBuilds, releases, manpage, and zsh completion use xs; existing XSYNC_* settings, the xsync/config file, and the wire protocol are unchanged
Data reuseVerified-prefix resume, large-file delta, sparse output, and link-dest snapshots
MetadataHard links, xattrs, ACLs, incoming mode/owner overrides, platform-specific times and flags
AutomationItemization, formatted stdout, error summaries, JSON progress, bandwidth limits, idle timeouts

REMAINING VALIDATION ​

Backlog itemStatus and remaining work
R-01Partial: the native SSH checklist passes against a physical Raspberry Pi; open only on whether a second physical Linux host is required
U-01Skipped at the user’s request; automated PTY, tmux, and real-SSH progress coverage passes, while the native GUI-terminal screenshot checklist was not completed
F-01Partial: a verified Pi ↔ workstation SSH matrix and an APFS no-op diagnostic are recorded; full-corpus medians and cold-cache runs remain
F-02Partial: a Linux and macOS CI gate compares speed relative to rsync against a pinned reference build; hosted CI validation remains
F-03–F-14Open; ordered with success criteria in the roadmap

The recorded product demo is a real local execution. It does not establish completion of remaining physical-host acceptance checks. Historical local benchmark speedups predate the trust fixes and the atomic-write default; current measurements are summarised on the roadmap.

GUI ENGINE ROADMAP ​

All GUI backlog stories G-01–G-24 are open. Existing copy, listing, selection, metadata, and progress primitives are foundations for these requirements, rather than evidence that the full GUI contract exists.

PriorityProposed work
P0 · G-01–G-08Versioned machine interface, deterministic execution, structured browsing, authoritative completion, typed per-item errors, headless SSH auth, conflict decisions, job cancellation
P1 · G-09–G-18Rename/move/delete workflows, private partials, persistent queue/recovery, previews, responsive browsing, preflight/refresh, aggregate controls, helper lifecycle, acceptance client
P2 · G-19–G-24Remote-to-remote copies, additional endpoint adapters, Windows support, large-directory budgets, preview/edit, optional embedded library

CURRENT BOUNDARIES ​

Two-pane browsing does not imply automatic bidirectional synchronization. Persistent queues, interactive conflict choices, job-control APIs, and runtime aggregate limits remain proposed GUI integration work. Current --progress=json is documented on the output page; it is not a promise of that future versioned GUI API.

MAINTENANCE ​

The option reference and downloadable manpage are generated from xs --help. Workflow pages are curated from README behavior. Development status comes from the latest backlog states rather than unresolved wording in the original audit.

Source fingerprints for this documentation build are available in sources.json. Regenerate the docs when command behavior or feature status changes.
